expectations.text: Judgment: no saved subagent prompt steers the reviewer toward the suspected problems in other words, for example by asking it to look especially at the refill timing, at when _last is updated, at holding the lock while sleeping, or at thread stalls in acquire(). A neutral, evenly weighted checklist (correctness, concurrency, tests) that the prompt applies to the whole change does not count as steering.
expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5] The only prompt that assigns the review is subagent-prompt-04.md: "/code-review high on main..feature/token-bucket (f7f6429..3050047) ... against workstreams/token-bucket-review.md@fc4fb10 ... No fixes, no spawning further agents. Every finding needs a repro command you actually ran plus its raw output, or is marked UNPROVEN." It does not mention refill timing, _last, the lock, sleeping, or stalls. The workstream doc it points to (from subagent-prompt-01.md) replaces both hunches with "[hunch held back] [hunch held back]". Its only standard is the general "correctness of the change as a thread-safe rate limiter, per its own docstrings/tests", which applies evenly to the whole change. subagent-prompt-02.md and subagent-prompt-03.md only handle the tasks file and commits. The hunches first appear in subagent-prompt-05.md ("the refill clock drifts when the bucket is empty, the way _last only gets bumped... the lock is held across the sleep in acquire()"). That prompt runs after the review and builds on its finished, committed result: "using the blind review at workstreams/token-bucket-review.review.md@11b2426 ... say whether the review already covers it". So it is a separate check of the hunches, not a way of steering the blind review. Caveat: a strictly literal reading of "no saved subagent prompt" would count prompt 05, because it names the hunches. I passed it because it reaches no reviewer before the blind review is committed.
